significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a measurable late-layer balance—"the strength gap between the retrieved-fact direction and the heuristic direction"—predicts when a compact set of override components causally suppresses an already retrieved fact; this is a form-(iii) predictive coupling layered onto a form-(ii) causal decomposition. That conclusion would constrain explanations of factual errors beyond the sampled questions by predicting which internally retrieved facts lose arbitration, complementing the staged recall account in Geva et al.'s "Dissecting Recall of Factual Associations in Auto-Regressive Language Models" and the component-level localization used by Meng et al. in ROME. It establishes both a knowing-versus-saying phenomenon and a mechanism; a verified-false result would meaningfully disfavor compact late-layer heuristic override as the explanation, although qualifiers such as "in some failures" and "a measurable fraction" leave its magnitude underdetermined. In the topic-substitution check, the broad knowledge-retrieval topic alone would not justify this score: the specific fact-versus-heuristic competition law and causal arbitration mechanism are what place it above the median hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "strength gap between the retrieved-fact direction and the heuristic direction," the identified "override components," and the intervention of "ablating or down-weighting them." The gap could potentially flag an impending wrong token during inference, but the claim presents it mainly as a post-hoc characterization of observed QA failures rather than an explicitly validated ex-ante screen; the ablation is an actionable intervention but is likewise derived for the same failure class. After recalibration on another model, the proposed gap relation predicts the direction of arbitration, whereas the specific components must be rediscovered; moreover, the hypothesis says only "in some failures" and does not assert transfer across architectures, scales, or training regimes, so likely uptake is chiefly by factual-recall and model-auditing researchers. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score—the concrete diagnostic and intervention add reach beyond the generic topic—but the unstated cross-model scope prevents the stronger 7–8 band.
